blueprint_topic: Management of Care — nephrology RN education, advocacy, and coordination for kidney-care treatment decisions
stem: A client with advanced chronic kidney disease is discussing kidney-replacement therapy (KRT) and comprehensive conservative care. Which action best reflects the nephrology RN's role?

options.A: Assess information needs, explain options in understandable terms, support the client's informed preferences, and coordinate questions and referrals with the kidney-care team.
options.B: Recommend the treatment modality the nurse believes best fits the client's expected outcomes, then ask the team to obtain consent for that plan.
options.C: Emphasize dialysis and transplant options first and introduce comprehensive conservative care after the client indicates that KRT is not preferred.
options.D: Provide treatment education after the nephrologist selects a plan, then begin advocacy and referral coordination once the treatment has been ordered.

rationale: A is correct. The American Nephrology Nurses Association describes the nephrology nurse as an advocate, educator, care coordinator, and direct caregiver who collaborates with the interprofessional team, helps patients obtain information, and supports the opportunity for informed consent in treatment decisions. KDIGO 2024 Practice Point 5.5.1 states that people with CKD should be informed about the options for KRT and comprehensive conservative care, and Practice Point 5.5.2 supports comprehensive conservative management for people who choose not to pursue KRT. B is incorrect because informed decision-making centers the client's preferences rather than having the RN select the modality. C is incorrect because current KDIGO guidance supports informing people about both KRT and comprehensive conservative care rather than withholding one option until another is declined. D is incorrect because nephrology nursing education, advocacy, and coordination are not limited to the period after another clinician has already selected and ordered a treatment plan.
educational_objective: Support kidney-care decisions by assessing learning needs, providing understandable information about KRT and comprehensive conservative care, advocating for the client's informed preferences, and coordinating questions and referrals with the interprofessional kidney-care team.
source_organization: American Nephrology Nurses Association (ANNA); Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO)
source_document_title: The Nephrology Nursing Specialty; Nephrology Nursing Scope and Standards of Practice, 9th Edition; KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease
source_version_date: ANNA current specialty/publications pages rechecked 2026-08-20; Nephrology Nursing Scope and Standards of Practice 9th edition ©2022 remains listed as the current scope/standards resource; KDIGO 2024 CKD guideline remains the current global standard, with a 2026 focused update limited to Chapter 3
source_locator: ANNA — The Nephrology Nursing Specialty: outpatient nephrology nurses function as advocates, educators, consultants, care coordinators, and direct caregivers; the nephrology nurse coordinates patient care with other providers/team members and acts as patient teacher and advocate, assists the patient in seeking information, assures opportunity for informed consent in treatment decisions, and promotes patient-desired independence. ANNA Publications: Nephrology Nursing Scope and Standards of Practice ©2022 (9th edition) remains listed as the current practice-scope resource. KDIGO 2024 CKD Guideline — Chapter 5, Section 5.5 Structure and process of supportive care and comprehensive conservative management, guideline page S268/PDF page 153: Practice Point 5.5.1, inform people with CKD about options for KRT and comprehensive conservative care; Practice Point 5.5.2, support comprehensive conservative management as an option for people who choose not to pursue KRT. KDIGO current guideline page states the 2024 CKD guideline remains the current global standard; the 2026 focused update concerns Chapter 3.
source_claim_supported: Current kidney-care guidance supports informing people with advanced CKD about KRT and comprehensive conservative care and preserving informed patient choice; current ANNA standards describe nephrology RN responsibilities that include education, advocacy, informed-consent support, and interprofessional care coordination rather than selecting the treatment modality for the client.
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care — Advocacy, Client Rights, Collaboration with Multidisciplinary Team, Referrals, Case Management, and Continuity of Care: discuss treatment options with the client and respect decisions; advocate for client needs/preferences; collaborate with multidisciplinary team members; assess referral/resource needs; act as liaison/coordinator; communicate unresolved questions to appropriate team members.
pdf_visual_verification: KDIGO 2024 CKD Guideline Chapter 5, Section 5.5 on guideline page S268/PDF page 153 was visually verified by screenshot on 2026-08-20, showing Practice Points 5.5.1 and 5.5.2. Relevant NCSBN 2026 Management of Care advocacy/client-rights/collaboration/referral content was visually verified earlier in this audit session; no unverified NCSBN screenshot claim is used here.
targeted_near_duplicate_check: Repository-targeted search for 'kidney replacement conservative care nephrology nurse education informed consent advocacy coordinator' returned no indexed matching files; no near-duplicate identified by the targeted check.
correction_summary: Rebuilt the cueable role-definition item into an RN action scenario. The key is shorter and role-bounded; distractors now test realistic errors involving clinician substitution for patient choice, delayed presentation of conservative care, and delaying nursing advocacy/coordination until after a treatment order.

option_audit.A: Correct; integrates ANNA-supported education/advocacy/coordination with KDIGO-supported balanced presentation of KRT and comprehensive conservative care.
option_audit.B: Plausible paternalistic role-boundary error; incorrect because the RN supports informed patient choice rather than selecting the modality for the client.
option_audit.C: Plausible sequencing error; incorrect because KDIGO supports informing people about both KRT and comprehensive conservative care rather than reserving conservative care for later disclosure.
option_audit.D: Plausible order-dependent-role error; incorrect because nephrology RN education, advocacy, and coordination are not deferred until after a treatment has already been selected and ordered.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on always/never/only/all/must-type absolutes.
cueing_audit.answer_length: All four options contain comparable treatment-decision detail; the key is not uniquely signaled by length.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four alternatives are parallel nephrology-care actions.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified after ANNA/KDIGO source-based reread and targeted repository search.

independent_second_pass: Fresh adversarial pass rechecked ANNA's current specialty-role page and current 9th-edition Scope/Standards listing; KDIGO 2024 Chapter 5 Practice Points 5.5.1 and 5.5.2 plus the 2026 focused-update scope; visual verification of KDIGO page S268; NCSBN Management of Care fit; stem-key alignment; all four alternatives; patient-choice versus RN-role boundaries; timing of conservative-care education; cueing; ambiguity; and near-duplicate risk.
